Encore 0.7: faster and lighter everywhere, with GPU drawing back on Linux and a native package for Fedora.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Encore_0.7.0_universal.dmg` |
| Windows 10 and 11 | `Encore_0.7.0_x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+ | `Encore_0.7.0_amd64.deb` |
| Fedora 40+ and other RPM systems (glibc 2.35+) | `Encore-0.7.0-1.x86_64.rpm` |
| Other Linux (glibc 2.35+) | `Encore_0.7.0_amd64.AppImage` |

Encore 0.5 and 0.6 update themselves to this version: they download it in
the background and install it the next time you quit, or right away with
**Restart to update**. Updating keeps your session, settings and downloads.
From 0.4 or earlier, download it from this page.

## First launch

These builds are not code-signed yet.

- **macOS:** a fresh download asks you to choose **Open Anyway** in **System
  Settings → Privacy & Security** once. After an update, macOS asks once
  again for access to your saved session in the Keychain; choose **Always
  Allow**.
- **Windows:** SmartScreen warns on first run. Choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**. If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks the app.
- **Fedora:** install with `sudo dnf install ./Encore-0.7.0-1.x86_64.rpm`.
  The `.rpm` uses your system's own WebKit and graphics drivers. Like the
  `.deb`, it doesn't update itself: Encore tells you when a new version is
  out and links to it.

## What's new

- **A package for Fedora.** The new `.rpm` installs Encore like any other
  Fedora app, with your system's WebKit instead of the one the AppImage
  carries.
- **Faster to start playing.**
  - Pressing Play no longer waits 400 ms before looking up the song.
  - Sound starts as soon as the first bytes arrive, instead of after the
    first megabyte. On a slow connection that's up to a second sooner.
  - The first song after launching Encore needs about a tenth of the work it
    did, because Encore now keeps what it learned from YouTube's player
    between launches.
- **Lighter while playing.** The seek bar, lyrics and colours now redraw
  only when they change, never every frame, and not at all while the window
  is hidden. The blurred cover behind the now playing panel and full-screen
  lyrics is made once per song instead of being blurred live.
- **GPU drawing on Linux.** The AppImage now keeps WebKit's GPU compositing.
  If your graphics driver crashes with it, Encore notices, restarts and
  draws without the GPU from then on.
- **Long playlists.** Finding, sorting and scrolling in long playlists use a
  fraction of the work and memory they did.
- **Less memory over long sessions.** Covers, page links and finished songs
  no longer pile up in memory, and covers download once even when several
  parts of the app ask for them.

## Fixes

- An audio download that a server answered with the wrong range could be
  saved as if it were complete. Encore now checks every range and fetches it
  again when it doesn't match.
- Seeking while the network stalled had to wait for the stalled download.
  It now answers at once.

Encore is unofficial and not affiliated with YouTube or Google.
